ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the entire setup is in a state of rest. The smooth pulley D is fixed on the inclined plane C. The light rope connecting block A has the segment $O D$ horizontal and the segment $D A$ parallel to the inclined plane. It is known that the mass of block A is $m_{A}=2.4\mathrm{kg}$, the mass of block B is $m_{B}=3.2\mathrm{kg}$, and the angle between the light rope $O E$ and the vertical direction, as well as the angle of the inclined plane, is $37^{\circ}$. The gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

1. The magnitude of the tension in ropes $OE$, $OD$.
2. The magnitude and direction of the frictional force exerted by inclined plane C on block A.
3. The magnitude of the frictional force exerted by the ground on C.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, at the fixed point E in the upper left, there is a section of inclined rope EO; the angle between EO and the vertical dashed line is labeled 37°; at the knot O, the rope divides into a rope segment vertically downward connecting block B and a rope segment OD horizontally to the right. D is a smooth pulley fixed near the upper end of inclined plane C, and after passing D, the rope connects to block A downward to the right along the direction of the inclined plane. Inclined plane C is placed on horizontal ground, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane is also labeled 37°. Calculate according to the specified method: 1. Analyze the forces on knot O. Block B is stationary, so the magnitude of the tension exerted by the vertical rope on O equals T_OB=m_B g=3.2×10=32 N, directed downward. The tension T_OE of the inclined rope OE makes an angle of 37° with the vertical direction, and the tension T_OD of the horizontal rope OD is horizontally to the right. The equilibrium conditions are: T_OE cos37°=32, T_OD=T_OE sin37°. Therefore T_OE=32/0.8=40 N, T_OD=40×0.6=24 N. 2. Pulley D is smooth and the rope is light, so the tension in rope segment DA is the same as OD: T_DA=24 N. Analyze block A along the direction of the inclined plane: the component of gravity down the inclined plane is m_A g sin37°=2.4×10×0.6=14.4 N; the rope tension 24 N is up the inclined plane. Since 24 N is greater than 14.4 N, the friction force must be down the inclined plane to maintain equilibrium. Its magnitude is f_A=24-14.4=9.6 N. 3. Analyze the horizontal forces on inclined plane C together with the fixed pulley D. The action of block A on inclined plane C includes friction and pressure. The friction force of the inclined plane on A is down the inclined plane, so the friction force of A on C is up the inclined plane, and its horizontal component is 9.6×0.8=7.68 N to the left. The magnitude of the pressure of A on C is N=m_A g cos37°=2.4×10×0.8=19.2 N, and its horizontal component is 19.2×0.6=11.52 N to the left. Therefore the total horizontal action of A on C is 7.68+11.52=19.2 N to the left. The pulley is subjected to the tensions of two sections of rope: the OD section gives the pulley 24 N to the left; the DA section gives the pulley 24 N downward to the right along the inclined plane, whose horizontal component is 24×0.8=19.2 N to the right. Therefore the resultant horizontal action of the rope on the pulley is 24-19.2=4.8 N to the left. Thus C is subjected in total to a horizontal external force of 19.2+4.8=24 N to the left, and the friction force of the ground on C should be 24 N to the right to keep it stationary.
